hypotheses.justification:
The statement does not mention simplicity: it only involves `S : Setting G`, `L`, `S.width`, `Nat.card S.Mbar`, `mbarModel`, `KPGL` and `pglM0`. All of these are defined for `[Group G] [Finite G]`.

The only use in the proof is the call `censusCond_conj S L false hw hL hminus hgQ hgne`. That lemma (T1216Census.lean, line 312) takes `[IsSimpleGroup G]`, but its proof does not use it. I read the whole proof, lines 312–427.

It only uses these lemmas, none of which assume simplicity:
- `S.cl_conj_z_ne_zero` and `S.q_cl_conj_z`
- `S.Lbar_le_Mbar`
- `S.s12_Lbar_apply_cl_a`
- `S.isElementaryAbelian_Lbar`
- `four_le_card_Lbar` and `eight_le_card_Lbar`, the private ones in the same file; their signatures have only `[Group G] [Finite G]`
- `S.timmesfeld_12_4_1` and `S.timmesfeld_12_4_2`
- generic `Subgroup` lemmas

The files holding the `Setting` lemmas (S12Basic, S12Cent, S3Qa, S4Defs, S3bConj) work under `variable {G} [Group G] [Finite G]`. `IsSimpleGroup` appears there only inside an `attribute [-instance]` line. MbarModel.lean (`conjL_ρ_mem_mbarModel`) has the same `[Group G] [Finite G]` setup.

The other steps do not use it either: `qtPlusType_of_card` takes only `[Group G] [Finite G]`, and the rest is generic group and linear algebra plus `hF`, `hK` and `hL`.

So `censusCond_conj` stays provable with its `[IsSimpleGroup G]` binder deleted, and the same proof works. Then `pgl_eq_z_of_commute` is provable without `[IsSimpleGroup G]` by the same proof.
